name: Battle of Kosovo
note: The accounts of this battle are scarce and differ, and they give no ground, so none is drawn. They do not say which way the armies faced; the Serbs are drawn on the left facing the Ottomans, which puts the Serbian left and the Ottoman right at the top. The accounts say that light Ottoman cavalry and light infantry counterattacked after the Serbian charge but do not place them, so that counter-blow is drawn from the left wing. The Ottoman camels and the death of Murad are not drawn: the accounts give conflicting versions of when and how he died. Army sizes are disputed and are not shown.

phases.title: The armies draw up on Kosovo Field
phases.text: Lazar held the Serbian centre, Branković the right and Vuković the left, with heavy cavalry in front. Murad stood behind his Janissaries in the centre, Bayezid held the Ottoman right, Yakub the left, and archers stood on both wings.
phases.quote: Prince Lazar led the Serb center, Branković took command of the right, and Vuković commanded the left

phases.title: Ottoman archers shoot at the Serbian cavalry
phases.text: The fighting began with Ottoman archers shooting at the Serbian cavalry, who then made ready to attack. The archers had been posted on the two wings of the Ottoman line.
phases.quote: the battle commenced with Ottoman archers shooting at Serbian cavalry, who then made ready for the attack

phases.title: The Serbian cavalry breaks the Ottoman left
phases.text: After forming a wedge, the Serbian cavalry charged and broke through the Ottoman left wing under Yakub. It was less successful against the centre and the right wing.
phases.quote: the Serbian cavalry managed to break through the Ottoman left wing, but were not as successful against the center and the right wing

phases.title: Ottoman light troops counterattack
phases.text: When the knights' charge was spent, light Ottoman cavalry and light infantry counterattacked, and the Serbian heavy armour became a disadvantage.
phases.quote: light Ottoman cavalry and light infantry counterattacked and the Serbian heavy armor became a disadvantage

phases.title: The Serbian centre pushes back the Ottomans
phases.text: In the centre the Serbian troops pushed the Ottomans back. Bayezid's wing barely held off the Bosnians under Vuković, who inflicted heavy losses on the Ottomans.
phases.quote: In the center, Serbian troops managed to push back Ottoman forces, except for Bayezid's wing, which barely held off the Bosnians

phases.title: Bayezid's counterattack pushes the Serbs back
phases.text: The Ottomans, in a ferocious counterattack led by Bayezid, pushed the Serbian forces back. The Janissaries came forward again in the centre.
phases.quote: The Ottomans, in a ferocious counterattack led by Bayezid, pushed the Serbian forces back and then prevailed later in the day, routing the Serbian infantry.

phases.title: The Serbian infantry is routed
phases.text: Later in the day the Ottomans prevailed and routed the Serbian infantry, which broke and fell back from the centre of the field.
phases.quote: then prevailed later in the day, routing the Serbian infantry.

phases.title: The Bosnians drift towards the centre
phases.text: Both flanks still held. Vuković's Bosnian troops drifted toward the centre to make up for the heavy losses of the Serbian infantry.
phases.quote: Both flanks still held, with Vuković's Bosnian troops drifting toward the center to compensate for the heavy losses inflicted on the Serbian infantry.

phases.title: Branković withdraws
phases.text: Branković saw that there was no hope of victory and withdrew from the field with as many of his men as he could save.
phases.quote: saw that there was no hope for victory and fled to save as many men as he could

phases.title: The remaining forces yield the field
phases.text: Some time after Branković's retreat the remaining Bosnian and Serbian forces gave up the field, believing that victory was no longer possible.
phases.quote: Sometime after Branković's retreat from the battle, the remaining Bosnian and Serb forces yielded the field
